title: Student Protests Over Education Standards Disrupt 700+ French Schools
summary:
Thousands of students in France have been demonstrating over education standards, and the protests have disrupted more than 700 schools. The protests began last week in the capital, Paris, and have spread across the country, with cities including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille affected. Education standards are the expectations about how well schools teach students and what they provide. The blockades and protests started last week before spreading to hundreds of schools. A blockade is when people block an entrance so that others cannot go in.

French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said 735 of France's 3,700 schools were now affected "one way or another" by the protests. He said things had "gone from high-school student demonstrations to a public order disturbance." A public order disturbance is a situation in which crowds disrupt normal life and police are called in.

Education Minister Édouard Geffray said the movement had been taken over by non-students. He told the broadcaster BFMTV that teachers had said, "the people in front of me were not my students."

The education ministry said at least 65 staff members were injured. It also reported "significant damage" to school facilities after attacks on school gates, entrances and fences. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 1,747 people were arrested on Friday.

One 16-year-old protester, Lola, told AFP that "our school is closed this morning." She said police actions had made things worse.

Officials and protesters describe the protests in different ways. Geffray says non-students have taken over the movement, while Lola says police actions have made students angrier.

The protests come six months before next year's presidential election, a crucial time for President Emmanuel Macron.
why_it_matters: Schools provide an important public service, and widespread disruption shows how strongly people can disagree about education and how governments respond.
